Question 1

6 points
Compute the area of the region bounded by y=x2−4x+6y = x^2 - 4x + 6y=x2−4x+6 and y=11y = 11y=11.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Find Where the Curves Meet

    Set the two equal: x2−4x+6=11x^2 - 4x + 6 = 11x2−4x+6=11, so x2−4x−5=0x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0x2−4x−5=0. This factors as (x−5)(x+1)=0(x - 5)(x + 1) = 0(x−5)(x+1)=0, so the curves meet at x=−1x = -1x=−1 and x=5x = 5x=5.

  2. Step 2: Decide Which Curve Is on Top

    Test a point between them, such as x=0x = 0x=0. The parabola gives 666 and the line gives 111111, so the line y=11y = 11y=11 is on top on the whole interval [−1,5][-1, 5][−1,5].

  3. Step 3: Set Up the Integral

    The area is the integral of the top curve minus the bottom curve:
    A=∫−15(11−(x2−4x+6)) dx=∫−15(−x2+4x+5) dx.A = \int_{-1}^{5} \big(11 - (x^2 - 4x + 6)\big)\,dx = \int_{-1}^{5} (-x^2 + 4x + 5)\,dx.A=∫−15​(11−(x2−4x+6))dx=∫−15​(−x2+4x+5)dx.
    A=∫−15(11−(x2−4x+6)) dx=∫−15(−x2+4x+5) dx.\begin{aligned}A &= \int_{-1}^{5} \big(11 - (x^2 - 4x + 6)\big)\,dx \\ &= \int_{-1}^{5} (-x^2 + 4x + 5)\,dx.\end{aligned}A​=∫−15​(11−(x2−4x+6))dx=∫−15​(−x2+4x+5)dx.​

  4. Step 4: Evaluate

    An antiderivative is −x33+2x2+5x-\tfrac{x^3}{3} + 2x^2 + 5x−3x3​+2x2+5x. At x=5x = 5x=5 it equals −1253+50+25=1003.-\tfrac{125}{3} + 50 + 25 = \tfrac{100}{3}.−3125​+50+25=3100​. At x=−1x = -1x=−1 it equals 13+2−5=−83\tfrac13 + 2 - 5 = -\tfrac8331​+2−5=−38​. Subtract: A=1003+83=1083=36.A = \tfrac{100}{3} + \tfrac{8}{3} = \tfrac{108}{3} = 36.A=3100​+38​=3108​=36.

Answer

A=36A = 36A=36

Question 2

6 points
Find the volume of the solid formed by revolving f(x)=xf(x) = \sqrt{x}f(x)=x​ about the yyy-axis on [0,9][0,9][0,9].
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Picture the Region

    The region being revolved is the area under y=xy = \sqrt{x}y=x​ and above the xxx-axis for 0≤x≤90 \le x \le 90≤x≤9. Revolving it about the yyy-axis sweeps out the solid.

  2. Step 2: Choose Shells

    The region is made of vertical strips and the axis is vertical, so cylindrical shells fit. The strip at xxx has radius xxx (its distance from the yyy-axis) and height x\sqrt{x}x​.

  3. Step 3: Set Up the Integral

    V=2π∫09xx dx=2π∫09x3/2 dx.V = 2\pi\int_0^9 x\sqrt{x}\,dx = 2\pi\int_0^9 x^{3/2}\,dx.V=2π∫09​xx​dx=2π∫09​x3/2dx.
    V=2π∫09xx dx=2π∫09x3/2 dx.\begin{aligned}V &= 2\pi\int_0^9 x\sqrt{x}\,dx \\ &= 2\pi\int_0^9 x^{3/2}\,dx.\end{aligned}V​=2π∫09​xx​dx=2π∫09​x3/2dx.​

  4. Step 4: Evaluate

    ∫09x3/2 dx=25x5/2∣09=25⋅243=4865,\int_0^9 x^{3/2}\,dx = \tfrac25 x^{5/2}\Big|_0^9 = \tfrac25 \cdot 243 = \tfrac{486}{5},∫09​x3/2dx=52​x5/2​09​=52​⋅243=5486​, because 95/2=35=2439^{5/2} = 3^5 = 24395/2=35=243. So V=2π⋅4865=972π5.V = 2\pi \cdot \tfrac{486}{5} = \tfrac{972\pi}{5}.V=2π⋅5486​=5972π​.

  5. Step 5: Check With Washers

    In yyy, the region runs from y=0y = 0y=0 to y=3y = 3y=3. At height yyy it stretches from x=y2x = y^2x=y2 to x=9x = 9x=9, so the washer has outer radius 999 and inner radius y2y^2y2:
    π∫03(81−y4) dy=π(243−2435)=972π5.\pi\int_0^3 (81 - y^4)\,dy = \pi\left(243 - \tfrac{243}{5}\right) = \tfrac{972\pi}{5}.π∫03​(81−y4)dy=π(243−5243​)=5972π​.
    π∫03(81−y4) dy=π(243−2435)=972π5.\begin{aligned}& \pi\int_0^3 (81 - y^4)\,dy \\ &= \pi\left(243 - \tfrac{243}{5}\right) \\ &= \tfrac{972\pi}{5}.\end{aligned}​π∫03​(81−y4)dy=π(243−5243​)=5972π​.​

Answer

V=972π5≈610.73V = \tfrac{972\pi}{5} \approx 610.73V=5972π​≈610.73

Question 3

6 points
Evaluate ∫0π/4cos⁡(2x) [1+sin⁡(2x)]3 dx.\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4} \cos(2x)\,[1 + \sin(2x)]^3\,dx.∫0π/4​cos(2x)[1+sin(2x)]3dx.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Choose the Substitution

    The expression inside the power is 1+sin⁡(2x)1 + \sin(2x)1+sin(2x), and its derivative 2cos⁡(2x)2\cos(2x)2cos(2x) appears outside up to a constant. Let u=1+sin⁡(2x)u = 1 + \sin(2x)u=1+sin(2x), so du=2cos⁡(2x) dxdu = 2\cos(2x)\,dxdu=2cos(2x)dx and cos⁡(2x) dx=12 du\cos(2x)\,dx = \tfrac12\,ducos(2x)dx=21​du.

  2. Step 2: Change the Limits

    When x=0x = 0x=0, u=1+sin⁡0=1u = 1 + \sin 0 = 1u=1+sin0=1. When x=π/4x = \pi/4x=π/4, u=1+sin⁡(π/2)=2u = 1 + \sin(\pi/2) = 2u=1+sin(π/2)=2.

  3. Step 3: Integrate

    In terms of uuu, the integral becomes
    12∫12u3 du=12⋅u44∣12=18(16−1)=158.\frac12\int_1^2 u^3\,du = \frac12\cdot\frac{u^4}{4}\Big|_1^2 = \frac18(16 - 1) = \frac{15}{8}.21​∫12​u3du=21​⋅4u4​​12​=81​(16−1)=815​.
    12∫12u3 du=12⋅u44∣12=18(16−1)=158.\begin{aligned}& \frac12\int_1^2 u^3\,du \\ &= \frac12\cdot\frac{u^4}{4}\Big|_1^2 \\ &= \frac18(16 - 1) \\ &= \frac{15}{8}.\end{aligned}​21​∫12​u3du=21​⋅4u4​​12​=81​(16−1)=815​.​

Answer

158=1.875\tfrac{15}{8} = 1.875815​=1.875

Question 4

6 points
Evaluate ∫9t e4t dt\displaystyle\int 9t\,e^{4t}\,dt∫9te4tdt by integration by parts. Write the full antiderivative.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Choose uuu and dvdvdv

    Pick u=9tu = 9tu=9t, because its derivative is simpler, and dv=e4t dtdv = e^{4t}\,dtdv=e4tdt. Then du=9 dtdu = 9\,dtdu=9dt and v=14e4tv = \tfrac14 e^{4t}v=41​e4t.

  2. Step 2: Apply the Formula

    Use ∫u dv=uv−∫v du\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du∫udv=uv−∫vdu:
    ∫9te4t dt=94te4t−∫94e4t dt.\int 9te^{4t}\,dt = \tfrac94 te^{4t} - \int \tfrac94 e^{4t}\,dt.∫9te4tdt=49​te4t−∫49​e4tdt.
    ∫9te4t dt=94te4t−∫94e4t dt.\begin{aligned}\int 9te^{4t}\,dt &= \tfrac94 te^{4t} - \int \tfrac94 e^{4t}\,dt.\end{aligned}∫9te4tdt​=49​te4t−∫49​e4tdt.​

  3. Step 3: Finish the Last Integral

    ∫94e4t dt=916e4t,\int \tfrac94 e^{4t}\,dt = \tfrac{9}{16}e^{4t},∫49​e4tdt=169​e4t, so the antiderivative is 94te4t−916e4t+C.\tfrac94 te^{4t} - \tfrac{9}{16}e^{4t} + C.49​te4t−169​e4t+C.

  4. Step 4: Check by Differentiating

    By the product rule, ddt[94te4t−916e4t]=94e4t+9te4t−94e4t=9te4t,\tfrac{d}{dt}\left[\tfrac94 te^{4t} - \tfrac{9}{16}e^{4t}\right] = \tfrac94 e^{4t} + 9te^{4t} - \tfrac94 e^{4t} = 9te^{4t},dtd​[49​te4t−169​e4t]=49​e4t+9te4t−49​e4t=9te4t, which is the integrand.

Answer

94te4t−916e4t+C=916(4t−1)e4t+C\tfrac94 te^{4t} - \tfrac{9}{16}e^{4t} + C = \tfrac{9}{16}(4t - 1)e^{4t} + C49​te4t−169​e4t+C=169​(4t−1)e4t+C

Question 5

6 points
Evaluate ∫csc⁡4(4w) dw\displaystyle\int \csc^4(4w)\,dw∫csc4(4w)dw. Write the full antiderivative.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Split Off csc⁡2\csc^2csc2

    Write csc⁡4(4w)=csc⁡2(4w)⋅csc⁡2(4w)\csc^4(4w) = \csc^2(4w)\cdot\csc^2(4w)csc4(4w)=csc2(4w)⋅csc2(4w) and replace one factor using csc⁡2=1+cot⁡2\csc^2 = 1 + \cot^2csc2=1+cot2. This gives csc⁡4(4w)=(1+cot⁡2(4w))csc⁡2(4w).\csc^4(4w) = \big(1 + \cot^2(4w)\big)\csc^2(4w).csc4(4w)=(1+cot2(4w))csc2(4w).

  2. Step 2: Substitute

    Let u=cot⁡(4w)u = \cot(4w)u=cot(4w). Then du=−4csc⁡2(4w) dwdu = -4\csc^2(4w)\,dwdu=−4csc2(4w)dw, so csc⁡2(4w) dw=−14 du\csc^2(4w)\,dw = -\tfrac14\,ducsc2(4w)dw=−41​du.

  3. Step 3: Integrate in uuu

    The integral becomes −14∫(1+u2) du-\tfrac14\int(1+u^2)\,du−41​∫(1+u2)du, which equals −14(u+u33)+C.-\tfrac14\left(u + \tfrac{u^3}{3}\right) + C.−41​(u+3u3​)+C.

  4. Step 4: Substitute Back

    Replace uuu with cot⁡(4w)\cot(4w)cot(4w): −cot⁡(4w)4−cot⁡3(4w)12+C.-\tfrac{\cot(4w)}{4} - \tfrac{\cot^3(4w)}{12} + C.−4cot(4w)​−12cot3(4w)​+C.

Answer

−cot⁡(4w)4−cot⁡3(4w)12+C-\dfrac{\cot(4w)}{4} - \dfrac{\cot^3(4w)}{12} + C−4cot(4w)​−12cot3(4w)​+C

Question 6

6 points
Evaluate ∫x9x2−4 dx\displaystyle\int \frac{x}{9x^2-4}\,dx∫9x2−4x​dx. Use a uuu-substitution.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Choose the Substitution

    The derivative of the denominator, 18x18x18x, is a constant multiple of the numerator. Let u=9x2−4u = 9x^2 - 4u=9x2−4, so du=18x dxdu = 18x\,dxdu=18xdx and x dx=118 dux\,dx = \tfrac{1}{18}\,duxdx=181​du.

  2. Step 2: Integrate

    ∫x9x2−4 dx=118∫duu=118ln⁡∣u∣+C.\int \frac{x}{9x^2-4}\,dx = \frac{1}{18}\int\frac{du}{u} = \frac{1}{18}\ln|u| + C.∫9x2−4x​dx=181​∫udu​=181​ln∣u∣+C.
    ∫x9x2−4 dx=118∫duu=118ln⁡∣u∣+C.\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{x}{9x^2-4}\,dx \\ &= \frac{1}{18}\int\frac{du}{u} \\ &= \frac{1}{18}\ln|u| + C.\end{aligned}​∫9x2−4x​dx=181​∫udu​=181​ln∣u∣+C.​

  3. Step 3: Substitute Back

    The answer is 118ln⁡∣9x2−4∣+C\tfrac{1}{18}\ln|9x^2 - 4| + C181​ln∣9x2−4∣+C. Keep the absolute value, because 9x2−49x^2 - 49x2−4 is negative when ∣x∣<23|x| < \tfrac23∣x∣<32​.

Answer

118ln⁡∣9x2−4∣+C\tfrac{1}{18}\ln|9x^2 - 4| + C181​ln∣9x2−4∣+C

Question 7

6 points
Determine whether ∫8∞3x4+cos⁡2xx dx\displaystyle\int_{8}^{\infty} \frac{\sqrt[4]{3x} + \cos^2 x}{x}\,dx∫8∞​x43x​+cos2x​dx converges.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Find the Dominant Term

    For large xxx, cos⁡2x\cos^2 xcos2x stays between 0 and 1, while 3x4\sqrt[4]{3x}43x​ keeps growing. So the integrand behaves like (3x)1/4x=31/4x−3/4\tfrac{(3x)^{1/4}}{x} = 3^{1/4}x^{-3/4}x(3x)1/4​=31/4x−3/4. Since p=34≤1p = \tfrac34 \le 1p=43​≤1, expect divergence, so look for a smaller function whose integral diverges.

  2. Step 2: Bound From Below

    Because cos⁡2x≥0\cos^2 x \ge 0cos2x≥0, every x≥8x \ge 8x≥8 satisfies
    3x4+cos⁡2xx≥(3x)1/4x=31/4x−3/4.\frac{\sqrt[4]{3x} + \cos^2 x}{x} \ge \frac{(3x)^{1/4}}{x} = 3^{1/4}x^{-3/4}.x43x​+cos2x​≥x(3x)1/4​=31/4x−3/4.
    3x4+cos⁡2xx≥(3x)1/4x=31/4x−3/4.\begin{aligned}& \frac{\sqrt[4]{3x} + \cos^2 x}{x} \\ &\ge \frac{(3x)^{1/4}}{x} \\ &= 3^{1/4}x^{-3/4}.\end{aligned}​x43x​+cos2x​≥x(3x)1/4​=31/4x−3/4.​

  3. Step 3: Check the Comparison Integral

    ∫8∞x−3/4 dx\int_8^\infty x^{-3/4}\,dx∫8∞​x−3/4dx is a ppp-integral with p=34≤1p = \tfrac34 \le 1p=43​≤1, so it diverges. Directly, ∫8bx−3/4 dx=4b1/4−4⋅81/4,\int_8^b x^{-3/4}\,dx = 4b^{1/4} - 4\cdot 8^{1/4},∫8b​x−3/4dx=4b1/4−4⋅81/4, which grows without bound.

  4. Step 4: Conclude

    The integrand is at least as large as a positive function whose integral diverges, so by the Comparison Test the given integral diverges. The bound has to go below the integrand: a bound from above by a divergent integral would prove nothing.

Answer

The integral diverges.

Question 8

6 points
Compute the arc length of y=13x3/2y = \tfrac13 x^{3/2}y=31​x3/2 on 0≤x≤120 \le x \le 120≤x≤12.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Differentiate

    y′=13⋅32x1/2=12x1/2,y' = \tfrac13\cdot\tfrac32 x^{1/2} = \tfrac12 x^{1/2},y′=31​⋅23​x1/2=21​x1/2, so (y′)2=x4(y')^2 = \tfrac{x}{4}(y′)2=4x​.

  2. Step 2: Set Up the Integral

    L=∫0121+(y′)2 dx=∫0121+x4 dx.L = \int_0^{12}\sqrt{1 + (y')^2}\,dx = \int_0^{12}\sqrt{1 + \tfrac{x}{4}}\,dx.L=∫012​1+(y′)2​dx=∫012​1+4x​​dx.
    L=∫0121+(y′)2 dx=∫0121+x4 dx.\begin{aligned}L &= \int_0^{12}\sqrt{1 + (y')^2}\,dx \\ &= \int_0^{12}\sqrt{1 + \tfrac{x}{4}}\,dx.\end{aligned}L​=∫012​1+(y′)2​dx=∫012​1+4x​​dx.​

  3. Step 3: Substitute

    Let u=1+x4u = 1 + \tfrac{x}{4}u=1+4x​, so du=14 dxdu = \tfrac14\,dxdu=41​dx and dx=4 dudx = 4\,dudx=4du. When x=0x = 0x=0, u=1u = 1u=1; when x=12x = 12x=12, u=4u = 4u=4. So L=4∫14u1/2 duL = 4\int_1^4 u^{1/2}\,duL=4∫14​u1/2du.

  4. Step 4: Evaluate

    L=4⋅23u3/2∣14=83(8−1)=563.L = 4\cdot\tfrac23 u^{3/2}\Big|_1^4 = \tfrac83(8 - 1) = \tfrac{56}{3}.L=4⋅32​u3/2​14​=38​(8−1)=356​.

Answer

L=563≈18.667L = \tfrac{56}{3} \approx 18.667L=356​≈18.667

Question 9

6 points
Find the centroid (xˉ,yˉ)(\bar x, \bar y)(xˉ,yˉ​) of the region bounded by y=x2y = x^2y=x2 and y=9y = 9y=9. Compute both coordinates.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Describe the Region

    The curves meet where x2=9x^2 = 9x2=9, at x=−3x = -3x=−3 and x=3x = 3x=3. The region is −3≤x≤3-3 \le x \le 3−3≤x≤3 with x2≤y≤9x^2 \le y \le 9x2≤y≤9. The problem does not limit it to the first quadrant, so use the whole region.

  2. Step 2: Find the Area

    A=∫−33(9−x2) dx=[9x−x33]−33=18−(−18)=36.A = \int_{-3}^{3} (9 - x^2)\,dx = \left[9x - \tfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^{3} = 18 - (-18) = 36.A=∫−33​(9−x2)dx=[9x−3x3​]−33​=18−(−18)=36.
    A=∫−33(9−x2) dx=[9x−x33]−33=18−(−18)=36.\begin{aligned}A &= \int_{-3}^{3} (9 - x^2)\,dx \\ &= \left[9x - \tfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^{3} \\ &= 18 - (-18) \\ &= 36.\end{aligned}A​=∫−33​(9−x2)dx=[9x−3x3​]−33​=18−(−18)=36.​

  3. Step 3: Find xˉ\bar xxˉ

    The region is symmetric about the yyy-axis, so xˉ=0\bar x = 0xˉ=0. The moment integral agrees: ∫−33x(9−x2) dx=0\int_{-3}^{3} x(9 - x^2)\,dx = 0∫−33​x(9−x2)dx=0, because the integrand is odd.

  4. Step 4: Set Up MxM_xMx​

    For a region between a lower curve y=g(x)y = g(x)y=g(x) and an upper curve y=f(x)y = f(x)y=f(x), the moment about the xxx-axis is Mx=∫12(f2−g2) dx.M_x = \int \tfrac12\big(f^2 - g^2\big)\,dx.Mx​=∫21​(f2−g2)dx. Here
    Mx=∫−3312(81−x4) dx.M_x = \int_{-3}^{3} \tfrac12\big(81 - x^4\big)\,dx.Mx​=∫−33​21​(81−x4)dx.

  5. Step 5: Evaluate and Divide

    Mx=12[81x−x55]−33=12(9725+9725)=9725.M_x = \tfrac12\left[81x - \tfrac{x^5}{5}\right]_{-3}^{3} = \tfrac12\left(\tfrac{972}{5} + \tfrac{972}{5}\right) = \tfrac{972}{5}.Mx​=21​[81x−5x5​]−33​=21​(5972​+5972​)=5972​. Then yˉ=MxA=972/536=275.\bar y = \tfrac{M_x}{A} = \tfrac{972/5}{36} = \tfrac{27}{5}.yˉ​=AMx​​=36972/5​=527​.

Answer

(xˉ,yˉ)=(0,275)(\bar x, \bar y) = \left(0, \tfrac{27}{5}\right)(xˉ,yˉ​)=(0,527​)

    y=(x+3)2+2(x+3)−5=x2+6x+9+2x+6−5=x2+8x+10.\begin{aligned}y &= (x + 3)^2 + 2(x + 3) - 5 \\ &= x^2 + 6x + 9 + 2x + 6 - 5 \\ &= x^2 + 8x + 10.\end{aligned}y​=(x+3)2+2(x+3)−5=x2+6x+9+2x+6−5=x2+8x+10.​

Question 11

6 points
Convert the polar equation r=6cos⁡θ−4sin⁡θr = 6\cos\theta - 4\sin\thetar=6cosθ−4sinθ to rectangular form. The result is a circle. Identify its center.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Multiply by rrr

    r2=6rcos⁡θ−4rsin⁡θr^2 = 6r\cos\theta - 4r\sin\thetar2=6rcosθ−4rsinθ. Multiplying by rrr creates rcos⁡θr\cos\thetarcosθ and rsin⁡θr\sin\thetarsinθ, which convert directly to xxx and yyy.

  2. Step 2: Convert

    Use r2=x2+y2r^2 = x^2 + y^2r2=x2+y2, x=rcos⁡θx = r\cos\thetax=rcosθ and y=rsin⁡θy = r\sin\thetay=rsinθ: x2+y2=6x−4yx^2 + y^2 = 6x - 4yx2+y2=6x−4y.

  3. Step 3: Complete the Squares

    Move everything to the left: x2−6x+y2+4y=0x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 4y = 0x2−6x+y2+4y=0. Add 999 and 444 to both sides:
    (x−3)2+(y+2)2=13.(x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 13.(x−3)2+(y+2)2=13.

Answer

(x−3)2+(y+2)2=13(x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 13(x−3)2+(y+2)2=13; center (3,−2)(3, -2)(3,−2), radius 13\sqrt{13}13​

Question 12

Question 15

6 points
Classify the series ∑n=0∞(−1)n+42n2+5.\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+4}}{2n^2 + 5}.n=0∑∞​2n2+5(−1)n+4​. Classify it as absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent.
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Test Absolute Convergence First

    Drop the sign: ∣an∣=12n2+5|a_n| = \tfrac{1}{2n^2 + 5}∣an​∣=2n2+51​. If ∑∣an∣\sum |a_n|∑∣an​∣ converges, the series is absolutely convergent and no further test is needed.

  2. Step 2: Compare

    For n≥1n \ge 1n≥1, 12n2+5≤12n2\tfrac{1}{2n^2 + 5} \le \tfrac{1}{2n^2}2n2+51​≤2n21​, and ∑12n2=12∑1n2\sum \tfrac{1}{2n^2} = \tfrac12\sum\tfrac{1}{n^2}∑2n21​=21​∑n21​ converges (p=2>1p = 2 > 1p=2>1). The n=0n = 0n=0 term is a single finite number and does not affect convergence.

  3. Step 3: Conclude

    ∑∣an∣\sum |a_n|∑∣an​∣ converges, so the series is absolutely convergent. The Alternating Series Test alone would show only that the series converges, not which kind of convergence it has.

Answer

Absolutely convergent.

The adjacent side is 25−x2\sqrt{25 - x^2}25−x2​, so cot⁡θ=adjacentopposite=25−x2x.\cot\theta = \tfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{opposite}} = \tfrac{\sqrt{25 - x^2}}{x}.cotθ=oppositeadjacent​=x25−x2​​.

By the quotient rule, the derivative of 25−x2x\tfrac{\sqrt{25 - x^2}}{x}x25−x2​​ has denominator x2x^2x2 and numerator −x25−x2⋅x−25−x2.\tfrac{-x}{\sqrt{25-x^2}}\cdot x - \sqrt{25-x^2}.25−x2​−x​⋅x−25−x2​. Over the common denominator 25−x2\sqrt{25 - x^2}25−x2​, that numerator is −x2−(25−x2)25−x2=−2525−x2.\tfrac{-x^2 - (25 - x^2)}{\sqrt{25-x^2}} = \tfrac{-25}{\sqrt{25-x^2}}.25−x2​−x2−(25−x2)​=25−x2​−25​. Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Choose the Interval

    Since sin⁡θ≥−1\sin\theta \ge -1sinθ≥−1, r≥0r \ge 0r≥0 for every θ\thetaθ, and the cardioid is traced exactly once as θ\thetaθ runs from 000 to 2π2\pi2π.

    A=12∫02πr2 dθ=12∫02π(3+3sin⁡θ)2 dθ.A = \frac12\int_0^{2\pi} r^2\,d\theta = \frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(3 + 3\sin\theta)^2\,d\theta.A=21​∫02π​r2dθ=21​∫02π​(3+3sinθ)2dθ.
    A=12∫02πr2 dθ=12∫02π(3+3sin⁡θ)2 dθ.\begin{aligned}A &= \frac12\int_0^{2\pi} r^2\,d\theta \\ &= \frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(3 + 3\sin\theta)^2\,d\theta.\end{aligned}A​=21​∫02π​r2dθ=21​∫02π​(3+3sinθ)2dθ.​
    Expand the square as (3+3sin⁡θ)2=9(1+2sin⁡θ+sin⁡2θ),(3 + 3\sin\theta)^2 = 9\left(1 + 2\sin\theta + \sin^2\theta\right),(3+3sinθ)2=9(1+2sinθ+sin2θ), so A=92∫02π(1+2sin⁡θ+sin⁡2θ)dθ.A = \tfrac92\int_0^{2\pi}\left(1 + 2\sin\theta + \sin^2\theta\right)d\theta.A=29​∫02π​(1+2sinθ+sin2θ)dθ.

    Over [0,2π][0, 2\pi][0,2π], sin⁡θ\sin\thetasinθ and cos⁡2θ\cos 2\thetacos2θ each integrate to 0. So ∫02π(32+2sin⁡θ−12cos⁡2θ)dθ=32⋅2π=3π.\int_0^{2\pi}\left(\tfrac32 + 2\sin\theta - \tfrac12\cos2\theta\right)d\theta = \tfrac32\cdot 2\pi = 3\pi.∫02π​(23​+2sinθ−21​cos2θ)dθ=23​⋅2π=3π.

Question 20

18 points
Find the Maclaurin series for f(x)=ln⁡(1+2x)f(x) = \ln(1+2x)f(x)=ln(1+2x), state its radius of convergence, and use the first three nonzero terms to approximate ln⁡(1.2)\ln(1.2)ln(1.2).
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: Differentiate and Expand

    f′(x)=21+2xf'(x) = \tfrac{2}{1 + 2x}f′(x)=1+2x2​. This is a geometric series with ratio −2x-2x−2x:
    21+2x=2∑n=0∞(−2x)n=2−4x+8x2−⋯ ,\frac{2}{1+2x} = 2\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-2x)^n = 2 - 4x + 8x^2 - \cdots,1+2x2​=2n=0∑∞​(−2x)n=2−4x+8x2−⋯,
    21+2x=2∑n=0∞(−2x)n=2−4x+8x2−⋯ ,\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{1+2x} &= 2\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-2x)^n \\ &= 2 - 4x + 8x^2 - \cdots,\end{aligned}1+2x2​​=2n=0∑∞​(−2x)n=2−4x+8x2−⋯,​
    valid when ∣2x∣<1|2x| < 1∣2x∣<1.

  2. Step 2: Integrate Term by Term

    f(0)=ln⁡1=0f(0) = \ln 1 = 0f(0)=ln1=0, so integrate from 0 with no added constant:
    ln⁡(1+2x)=∑n=1∞(−1)n+1(2x)nn.\ln(1 + 2x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(2x)^n}{n}.ln(1+2x)=n=1∑∞​n(−1)n+1(2x)n​.
    Written out, the series begins 2x−2x2+83x3−4x4+⋯2x - 2x^2 + \tfrac83 x^3 - 4x^4 + \cdots2x−2x2+38​x3−4x4+⋯.

  3. Step 3: State the Radius

    The geometric series needs ∣2x∣<1|2x| < 1∣2x∣<1, that is ∣x∣<12|x| < \tfrac12∣x∣<21​. Integrating term by term does not change the radius, so R=12R = \tfrac12R=21​. The Ratio Test gives the same result, since the ratio of terms tends to 2∣x∣2|x|2∣x∣.

  4. Step 4: Pick the Value of xxx

    1+2x=1.21 + 2x = 1.21+2x=1.2 gives x=0.1x = 0.1x=0.1, which is inside the interval of convergence.

  5. Step 5: Approximate

    The first three nonzero terms at x=0.1x = 0.1x=0.1 are 2(0.1)−2(0.1)2+83(0.1)3=0.2−0.02+0.002667=0.182667.2(0.1) - 2(0.1)^2 + \tfrac83(0.1)^3 = 0.2 - 0.02 + 0.002667 = 0.182667.2(0.1)−2(0.1)2+38​(0.1)3=0.2−0.02+0.002667=0.182667. A calculator gives ln⁡1.2≈0.182322\ln 1.2 \approx 0.182322ln1.2≈0.182322, and the difference is smaller than the next term's size, 4(0.1)4=0.00044(0.1)^4 = 0.00044(0.1)4=0.0004.

ln⁡(1+2x)=∑n=1∞(−1)n+1(2x)nn,\ln(1+2x) = \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(2x)^n}{n},ln(1+2x)=n=1∑∞​n(−1)n+1(2x)n​, R=12R = \tfrac12R=21​, and ln⁡(1.2)≈0.18267\ln(1.2) \approx 0.18267ln(1.2)≈0.18267

So lim⁡b→∞I(b)=14\lim_{b\to\infty} I(b) = \tfrac14limb→∞​I(b)=41​.

  5. Step 5: (c) Set Up the Equation

    I(b)=18I(b) = \tfrac18I(b)=81​ means 1+2ln⁡b4b2=18\tfrac{1 + 2\ln b}{4b^2} = \tfrac184b21+2lnb​=81​, which simplifies to 1+2ln⁡b=b221 + 2\ln b = \tfrac{b^2}{2}1+2lnb=2b2​. The equation mixes ln⁡b\ln blnb with b2b^2b2, so no algebra step isolates bbb; solve it numerically.

  6. Step 6: (c) Bracket the Root

    Let h(b)=2ln⁡b−b22+1h(b) = 2\ln b - \tfrac{b^2}{2} + 1h(b)=2lnb−2b2​+1. Then h(2)≈0.386>0h(2) \approx 0.386 > 0h(2)≈0.386>0 and h(2.5)≈−0.292<0h(2.5) \approx -0.292 < 0h(2.5)≈−0.292<0, so a root lies between 2 and 2.5. It is the only root with b>1b > 1b>1: h(1)=12h(1) = \tfrac12h(1)=21​, hhh increases until b=2b = \sqrt2b=2​, and then it decreases for good.

  7. Step 7: (c) Refine With Newton's Method

    h′(b)=2b−bh'(b) = \tfrac2b - bh′(b)=b2​−b, and Newton's method repeats bk+1=bk−h(bk)h′(bk)b_{k+1} = b_k - \tfrac{h(b_k)}{h'(b_k)}bk+1​=bk​−h′(bk​)h(bk​)​. Starting from b0=2b_0 = 2b0​=2 gives b1≈2.3863b_1 \approx 2.3863b1​≈2.3863, b2≈2.3167b_2 \approx 2.3167b2​≈2.3167 and b3≈2.3145b_3 \approx 2.3145b3​≈2.3145. So b≈2.314b \approx 2.314b≈2.314. A table of values or bisection reaches the same answer.

  8. Step 8: (d) Explain the Convergence

    For x≥1x \ge 1x≥1, ln⁡x≤x\ln x \le xlnx≤x, so 0≤ln⁡xx3≤1x2.0 \le \tfrac{\ln x}{x^3} \le \tfrac{1}{x^2}.0≤x3lnx​≤x21​. The integral ∫1∞x−2 dx\int_1^\infty x^{-2}\,dx∫1∞​x−2dx converges (p=2>1p = 2 > 1p=2>1), so by the Comparison Test the improper integral is finite. The finite limit 14\tfrac1441​ from part (b) shows the same thing directly.

(a) I(b)=14−1+2ln⁡b4b2;I(b) = \tfrac14 - \tfrac{1 + 2\ln b}{4b^2};I(b)=41​−4b21+2lnb​; (b) 14\tfrac1441​; (c) b≈2.314b \approx 2.314b≈2.314; (d) ln⁡xx3≤1x2\tfrac{\ln x}{x^3} \le \tfrac{1}{x^2}x3lnx​≤x21​ and ∫1∞x−2 dx\int_1^\infty x^{-2}\,dx∫1∞​x−2dx converges (or cite the finite limit in (b)).

Question 22

44 points
Consider the polar curve r=6cos⁡θr = 6\cos\thetar=6cosθ.
Complete all four parts: (a) (9 pts) Convert to Cartesian form and describe the shape. (b) (12 pts) Compute the area enclosed by the curve. (c) (14 pts) Compute the arc length of the curve on [0,π][0, \pi][0,π]. (d) (9 pts) Why does integrating over [0,2π][0, 2\pi][0,2π] overcount the enclosed area?
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: (a) Convert to Cartesian Form

    Multiply by rrr: r2=6rcos⁡θr^2 = 6r\cos\thetar2=6rcosθ, so x2+y2=6xx^2 + y^2 = 6xx2+y2=6x. Complete the square in xxx: (x−3)2+y2=9(x - 3)^2 + y^2 = 9(x−3)2+y2=9.

  2. Step 2: (a) Describe the Shape

    The curve is a circle with center (3,0)(3, 0)(3,0) and radius 3. It passes through the origin.

  3. Step 3: (b) Find One Full Trace

    At θ=0\theta = 0θ=0 the point is (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0). At θ=π/2\theta = \pi/2θ=π/2, r=0r = 0r=0, so the curve passes through the origin. At θ=π\theta = \piθ=π, r=−6r = -6r=−6, and a negative rrr is plotted on the opposite side of the origin, so the point is (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0) again. So 0≤θ≤π0 \le \theta \le \pi0≤θ≤π traces the circle exactly once.

  4. Step 4: (b) Compute the Area

    A=12∫0π36cos⁡2θ dθ=18∫0π1+cos⁡2θ2 dθ=9[θ+sin⁡2θ2]0π=9π.A = \frac12\int_0^{\pi} 36\cos^2\theta\,d\theta = 18\int_0^{\pi}\frac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}\,d\theta = 9\left[\theta + \frac{\sin 2\theta}{2}\right]_0^{\pi} = 9\pi.A=21​∫0π​36cos2θdθ=18∫0π​21+cos2θ​dθ=9[θ+2sin2θ​]0π​=9π.
    A=12∫0π36cos⁡2θ dθ=18∫0π1+cos⁡2θ2 dθ=9[θ+sin⁡2θ2]0π=9π.\begin{aligned}A &= \frac12\int_0^{\pi} 36\cos^2\theta\,d\theta \\ &= 18\int_0^{\pi}\frac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}\,d\theta \\ &= 9\left[\theta + \frac{\sin 2\theta}{2}\right]_0^{\pi} \\ &= 9\pi.\end{aligned}A​=21​∫0π​36cos2θdθ=18∫0π​21+cos2θ​dθ=9[θ+2sin2θ​]0π​=9π.​
    This matches the area of a circle of radius 3, π⋅32\pi\cdot 3^2π⋅32.

  5. Step 5: (c) Set Up the Arc Length

    The polar arc length formula is L=∫r2+(drdθ)2 dθ.L = \int\sqrt{r^2 + \left(\tfrac{dr}{d\theta}\right)^2}\,d\theta.L=∫r2+(dθdr​)2​dθ. Here drdθ=−6sin⁡θ\tfrac{dr}{d\theta} = -6\sin\thetadθdr​=−6sinθ, so r2+(drdθ)2=36cos⁡2θ+36sin⁡2θ=36.r^2 + \left(\tfrac{dr}{d\theta}\right)^2 = 36\cos^2\theta + 36\sin^2\theta = 36.r2+(dθdr​)2=36cos2θ+36sin2θ=36.

  6. Step 6: (c) Evaluate

    L=∫0π6 dθ=6πL = \int_0^{\pi} 6\,d\theta = 6\piL=∫0π​6dθ=6π, which is the circumference of a circle of radius 3.

  7. Step 7: (d) Explain the Overcount

    For π≤θ≤2π\pi \le \theta \le 2\piπ≤θ≤2π the curve repeats itself. Since 6cos⁡(θ+π)=−6cos⁡θ6\cos(\theta + \pi) = -6\cos\theta6cos(θ+π)=−6cosθ, the point at angle θ+π\theta + \piθ+π has radius −r-r−r, and the point (−r,θ+π)(-r, \theta + \pi)(−r,θ+π) is the same point as (r,θ)(r, \theta)(r,θ). So the circle is traced a second time, and 12∫02πr2 dθ=18π\tfrac12\int_0^{2\pi} r^2\,d\theta = 18\pi21​∫02π​r2dθ=18π counts the disk twice.

Answer

(a) (x−3)2+y2=9(x - 3)^2 + y^2 = 9(x−3)2+y2=9, a circle with center (3,0)(3, 0)(3,0) and radius 3; (b) 9π9\pi9π; (c) 6π6\pi6π; (d) the circle is traced twice on [0,2π][0, 2\pi][0,2π], giving 18π18\pi18π.

Question 23

44 points
Let f(x)=12−xf(x) = \dfrac{1}{2 - x}f(x)=2−x1​.
Complete all four parts: (a) (8 pts) Write f(x)f(x)f(x) as a power series about x=0x = 0x=0 and state its radius of convergence. Show worked solution

    Factor out 2 to get the form 11−ratio\tfrac{1}{1 - \text{ratio}}1−ratio1​:
    12−x=12⋅11−x/2=12∑n=0∞(x2)n=∑n=0∞xn2n+1.\frac{1}{2 - x} = \frac12\cdot\frac{1}{1 - x/2} = \frac12\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^n = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{2^{n+1}}.2−x1​=21​⋅1−x/21​=21​n=0∑∞​(2x​)n=n=0∑∞​2n+1xn​.
    12−x=12⋅11−x/2=12∑n=0∞(x2)n=∑n=0∞xn2n+1.\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2 - x} &= \frac12\cdot\frac{1}{1 - x/2} \\ &= \frac12\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^n \\ &= \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{2^{n+1}}.\end{aligned}2−x1​​=21​⋅1−x/21​=21​n=0∑∞​(2x​)n=n=0∑∞​2n+1xn​.​

  2. Step 2: (a) State the Radius

    A geometric series converges when its ratio has absolute value less than 1. Here ∣x2∣<1\left|\tfrac{x}{2}\right| < 1​2x​​<1 means ∣x∣<2|x| < 2∣x∣<2, so R=2R = 2R=2.

  3. Step 3: (b) Connect ggg to fff

    g(x)=ln⁡2−ln⁡(2−x)g(x) = \ln 2 - \ln(2 - x)g(x)=ln2−ln(2−x), so g′(x)=12−x=f(x)g'(x) = \tfrac{1}{2 - x} = f(x)g′(x)=2−x1​=f(x), and g(0)=ln⁡1=0g(0) = \ln 1 = 0g(0)=ln1=0.

  4. Step 4: (b) Integrate Term by Term

    Because g(0)=0g(0) = 0g(0)=0, g(x)=∫0xf(t) dtg(x) = \int_0^x f(t)\,dtg(x)=∫0x​f(t)dt with no added constant:
    g(x)=∑n=0∞xn+1(n+1) 2n+1.g(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^{n+1}}{(n+1)\,2^{n+1}}.g(x)=n=0∑∞​(n+1)2n+1xn+1​.
    Written out, the series begins x2+x28+x324+x464+⋯ ,\tfrac{x}{2} + \tfrac{x^2}{8} + \tfrac{x^3}{24} + \tfrac{x^4}{64} + \cdots,2x​+8x2​+24x3​+64x4​+⋯, and it converges for ∣x∣<2|x| < 2∣x∣<2.

  5. Step 5: (c) Substitute x=2/3x = 2/3x=2/3

    Write the term with m=n+1m = n + 1m=n+1 as 1m(x2)m\tfrac{1}{m}\left(\tfrac{x}{2}\right)^mm1​(2x​)m. At x=23x = \tfrac23x=32​, x2=13\tfrac{x}{2} = \tfrac132x​=31​, so the first four terms are
    13+118+181+1324=131324≈0.404321.\frac13 + \frac{1}{18} + \frac{1}{81} + \frac{1}{324} = \frac{131}{324} \approx 0.404321.31​+181​+811​+3241​=324131​≈0.404321.
    13+118+181+1324=131324≈0.404321.\begin{aligned}& \frac13 + \frac{1}{18} \\ &\quad + \frac{1}{81} \\ &\quad + \frac{1}{324} \\ &= \frac{131}{324} \\ &\approx 0.404321.\end{aligned}​31​+181​+811​+3241​=324131​≈0.404321.​
    The exact value is g(2/3)=ln⁡32≈0.405465g(2/3) = \ln\tfrac32 \approx 0.405465g(2/3)=ln23​≈0.405465.

  6. Step 6: (d) Write the Error as a Tail

    The error is everything after the fourth term: R4=∑m=5∞1m(13)m.R_4 = \sum_{m=5}^{\infty}\tfrac{1}{m}\left(\tfrac13\right)^m.R4​=∑m=5∞​m1​(31​)m. Every term is positive, so this series does not alternate, and the first omitted term alone is not a bound on the error.

  7. Step 7: (d) Bound the Tail by a Geometric Series

    For m≥5m \ge 5m≥5, 1m≤15\tfrac1m \le \tfrac15m1​≤51​, so
    R4≤15∑m=5∞(13)m=15⋅(1/3)51−1/3=1810≈0.00123.R_4 \le \frac15\sum_{m=5}^{\infty}\left(\frac13\right)^m = \frac15\cdot\frac{(1/3)^5}{1 - 1/3} = \frac{1}{810} \approx 0.00123.R4​≤51​m=5∑∞​(31​)m=51​⋅1−1/3(1/3)5​=8101​≈0.00123.
    R4≤15∑m=5∞(13)m=15⋅(1/3)51−1/3=1810≈0.00123.\begin{aligned}R_4 &\le \frac15\sum_{m=5}^{\infty}\left(\frac13\right)^m \\ &= \frac15\cdot\frac{(1/3)^5}{1 - 1/3} \\ &= \frac{1}{810} \\ &\approx 0.00123.\end{aligned}R4​​≤51​m=5∑∞​(31​)m=51​⋅1−1/3(1/3)5​=8101​≈0.00123.​

Section 4: Synthesis Question

This section has one multi-part problem that pulls several units together.

Question 24

40 points
A water tank lies on its side (oriented horizontally), and every slice perpendicular to its horizontal axis is the same cross-section. That cross-section is bounded by y=9−x2y = 9 - x^2y=9−x2 and the xxx-axis (x and y in meters; the x-axis is the flat bottom of the tank). The tank is 6 m long. Water fills it to y=5y = 5y=5. Assume ρ=1000 kg/m3\rho = 1000\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}ρ=1000kg/m3 and g=9.8 m/s2g = 9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}g=9.8m/s2.
Complete all parts: (a) (18 pts) Volume of water (cross-section integration). (b) (6 pts) Weight of water (in newtons). (c) (6 pts) xxx-coordinate of the centroid of the water's cross-section (the part of the cross-section below the water line); justify your answer. (d) (10 pts) Which Calculus II technique(s) did you use in each part, and what made each appropriate?
Show worked solution

  1. Step 1: (a) Describe the Water Region

    In one cross-section, the water fills the part of the parabola's region with 0≤y≤50 \le y \le 50≤y≤5. The water line y=5y = 5y=5 meets y=9−x2y = 9 - x^2y=9−x2 where x2=4x^2 = 4x2=4, at x=±2x = \pm 2x=±2. At height yyy, the parabola spans −9−y≤x≤9−y-\sqrt{9 - y} \le x \le \sqrt{9 - y}−9−y​≤x≤9−y​, so the water is 29−y2\sqrt{9 - y}29−y​ meters wide.

  2. Step 2: (a) Integrate Horizontal Strips

    Horizontal strips avoid splitting the region at x=±2x = \pm 2x=±2:
    A=∫0529−y dy.A = \int_0^5 2\sqrt{9 - y}\,dy.A=∫05​29−y​dy.
    Let u=9−yu = 9 - yu=9−y, so du=−dydu = -dydu=−dy, and the limits y=0y = 0y=0 and y=5y = 5y=5 become u=9u = 9u=9 and u=4u = 4u=4:
    A=∫492u1/2 du=43u3/2∣49=43(27−8)=763 m2.A = \int_4^9 2u^{1/2}\,du = \frac43 u^{3/2}\Big|_4^9 = \frac43(27 - 8) = \frac{76}{3}\ \text{m}^2.A=∫49​2u1/2du=34​u3/2​49​=34​(27−8)=376​ m2.
    A=∫492u1/2 du=43u3/2∣49=43(27−8)=763 m2.\begin{aligned}A &= \int_4^9 2u^{1/2}\,du \\ &= \frac43 u^{3/2}\Big|_4^9 \\ &= \frac43(27 - 8) \\ &= \frac{76}{3}\ \text{m}^2.\end{aligned}A​=∫49​2u1/2du=34​u3/2​49​=34​(27−8)=376​ m2.​

  3. Step 3: (a) Check With Vertical Strips

    For ∣x∣≤2|x| \le 2∣x∣≤2 the water is 5 m deep, and for 2≤∣x∣≤32 \le |x| \le 32≤∣x∣≤3 it reaches only the parabola. Since ∫23(9−x2) dx=9−193=83,\int_2^3 (9 - x^2)\,dx = 9 - \tfrac{19}{3} = \tfrac83,∫23​(9−x2)dx=9−319​=38​,
    A=2[∫025 dx+∫23(9−x2) dx]=2[10+83]=763 m2.A = 2\left[\int_0^2 5\,dx + \int_2^3 (9 - x^2)\,dx\right] = 2\left[10 + \tfrac83\right] = \tfrac{76}{3}\ \text{m}^2.A=2[∫02​5dx+∫23​(9−x2)dx]=2[10+38​]=376​ m2.
    A=2[∫025 dx+∫23(9−x2) dx]=2[10+83]=763 m2.\begin{aligned}A &= 2\left[\int_0^2 5\,dx + \int_2^3 (9 - x^2)\,dx\right] \\ &= 2\left[10 + \tfrac83\right] \\ &= \tfrac{76}{3}\ \text{m}^2.\end{aligned}A​=2[∫02​5dx+∫23​(9−x2)dx]=2[10+38​]=376​ m2.​

  4. Step 4: (a) Multiply by the Length

    Every slice along the 6 m length has this same area, so V=6A=6⋅763=152 m3.V = 6A = 6\cdot\tfrac{76}{3} = 152\ \text{m}^3.V=6A=6⋅376​=152 m3.

  5. Step 5: (b) Find the Weight

    The mass is m=ρV=1000×152=152,000m = \rho V = 1000 \times 152 = 152{,}000m=ρV=1000×152=152,000 kg. The weight is W=mg=152,000×9.8=1,489,600W = mg = 152{,}000 \times 9.8 = 1{,}489{,}600W=mg=152,000×9.8=1,489,600 N, about 1.49×1061.49 \times 10^61.49×106 N.

  6. Step 6: (c) Use Symmetry

    The water's cross-section is symmetric about the yyy-axis: each point (x,y)(x, y)(x,y) in it pairs with (−x,y)(-x, y)(−x,y). To justify xˉ=0\bar x = 0xˉ=0 with a moment, let h(x)h(x)h(x) be the water depth at xxx (h=5h = 5h=5 for ∣x∣≤2|x| \le 2∣x∣≤2 and h=9−x2h = 9 - x^2h=9−x2 for 2≤∣x∣≤32 \le |x| \le 32≤∣x∣≤3). Then My=∫−33x h(x) dx=0M_y = \int_{-3}^{3} x\,h(x)\,dx = 0My​=∫−33​xh(x)dx=0, because hhh is even, so x h(x)x\,h(x)xh(x) is odd. So xˉ=MyA=0\bar x = \tfrac{M_y}{A} = 0xˉ=AMy​​=0.

  7. Step 7: (d) Name the Techniques

    In part (a), slicing fits because the tank has the same cross-section along its whole length, so volume is area times length; the area is an integral evaluated by a uuu-substitution. In part (b), weight is density times ggg times volume (W=ρgVW = \rho g VW=ρgV), because the water has uniform density. In part (c), moments and centroids (xˉ=My/A\bar x = M_y / Axˉ=My​/A) apply, and symmetry makes My=0M_y = 0My​=0.

Answer

(a) V=152 m3V = 152\ \text{m}^3V=152 m3 (cross-section area 763 m2\tfrac{76}{3}\ \text{m}^2376​ m2); (b) W=1,489,600W = 1{,}489{,}600W=1,489,600 N; (c) xˉ=0\bar x = 0xˉ=0 by symmetry; (d) slicing with a uuu-substitution, W=ρgVW = \rho g VW=ρgV, and moments with symmetry.
